title: Expanding the galactose oxidase substrate repertoire via a multi-modal computational strategy.
summary: The model identified active galactose-oxidase variants across 13 structurally diverse secondary alcohols despite training on one substrate, with 77% precision; it also achieved 100% precision on a limited combinatorial-mutant library and yielded experimentally active starting-point variants for functional-ingredient synthesis. Primary article reports experimental screening of variants and independent experimental validation of prioritized candidates. The 100% precision result applies only to a limited combinatorial library; the output is a curated starting panel, not a finished industrial enzyme.
ai_technology: A multi-modal model integrated substrate-binding, protein-stability and aggregation descriptors to rank enzyme variants and select active candidates for experimental testing across previously untested secondary alcohol substrates.

source_review.scope: Read the primary PMC article’s indexed Results/Methods text, including the mutational-screen baseline, multi-modal model evaluation, and experimental validation. The model integrates substrate-binding, stability and aggregation descriptors, trained on one substrate, and identifies active variants across 13 structurally diverse secondary alcohols (77% precision); it generalizes to a limited combinatorial library (100% precision) and experimental assays produce candidate enzyme variants for functional-ingredient synthesis. The limited combinatorial library and precision-based selection are material caveats.
